method: Fresh seven-shot anonymous A/B review. Quality winner was chosen before reading the side map; side identity was recorded afterward.

shots.gap: The road composition is recognizable, but ours has card-like vegetation, broad hard-edged shoulder planes, and much shallower near/mid/far terrain depth than the continuous reference landscape.
Ours is washed out with a weak golden-hour read and little long-shadow land detail; the bar has warm directional light, rich ground color, and readable distant ridges.
Ours is too dark and lacks a convincing headlight cone, reflective road response, and readable night landform; the bar keeps the road and bend legible under headlights.

na_dimensions: exact weather/season semantics differ from the daytime cockpit bar
shots.gap: Ours has a recognizable cockpit but simplified low-detail dash and windshield framing; it lacks the bar's mirror, guardrail, road markings, and natural hillside materials.

Winter semantics are materially improved: ours is now clearly a terrestrial snowy road with leafless trees and snow-covered verges. It still lacks the bar's layered snowy hills, grey atmospheric falloff, active snowfall, and natural snow-road contact; a residual blue horizon makes it read as a clear overlay rather than a snow-weather world.

Ours provides an elevated winding road but remains a low-poly green valley with flat depth cues and no convincing water/shoreline; the bar has natural cut slopes, water, and layered atmospheric relief.
The driver framing is present, but ours has a simplified interior and generic road/vegetation; the bar has a detailed mirror, guardrail, lane treatment, and more grounded terrain materials.

max_gap: Continuous grounded landscape integration remains the largest mismatch: hard-edged shoulder/snow planes and stamped low-poly foliage prevent the bar's natural near/mid/far material depth. Winter semantics improved clearly, but winter atmosphere and snow material integration remain visibly behind.
notes: All seven captures completed at 1920x1080 with no page errors and full residency.
